name: Leghorn
lede: Leghorn is the pale yellow of bleached straw, named for the Italian port that gave its name to a famous straw hat.

sections.title: A hat and a port
sections.body:
Paterson gives leghorn as the yellow of straw, from Leghorn, the old English name of the Italian city now called Livorno [1]. The city produced a particular kind of wheat, and its straw was made into Leghorn hats and bonnets [1]. The swatch is a soft, warm cream-yellow, the kind of tone straw takes once it is bleached [3]. Paterson files the name among the yellows rather than the browns [2].

The straw itself was green when harvested, and it was bleached before use, so the color is a made color, not the raw plant's [1].

sections.title: Among the straws
sections.body: Paterson indexes leghorn with the yellows, beside [[straw]], [[maize]] and [[wheat]] [2]. The library ranks the same family close to this swatch [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No usable archive measurements exist for this name, so there is no painting data to quote [3]. The swatch is one screen reading of the name [3].
